key_insight: Machine learning can accurately predict and help optimize the strength and hardness of AA6082–AA7075 friction stir welded joints from welding parameters.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that data-driven models can support faster, smarter selection of friction stir welding settings for stronger, more consistent lightweight aluminum joints.
method: Inputs: tool rotational speed, traverse speed, and plunge depth.
Outputs: ultimate tensile strength and micro-hardness.
Compared LR, RF, SVR, XGBoost, and KNN using an 80:20 train-test split.
evidence_signal: Random Forest gave the best UTS prediction with testing MAE/RMSE of 9.007 MPa and 12.975 MPa, while RBF-SVR best predicted micro-hardness with MAE/RMSE of 0.923 HV and 1.155 HV.
watch_item: The results are based on a limited experimental dataset, so broader validation is needed before deployment across different materials, tool geometries, or welding setups.
paper_title: Explainable machine learning approach for predicting mechanical characteristics of AA6082–AA7075 friction stir welded joints
